candidates.rationale: Persistent above-fast-baseline trading days mark a building accumulation/distribution phase rather than a one-day spike; sustained participation growth precedes continued price adjustment as more traders become aware of the name.

A rising short-vs-long average-volume ratio captures the early acceleration phase of a liquidity/attention shock before it is fully reflected in price, since order flow typically leads full price discovery.

A stock whose relative liquidity standing among peers churns a lot is drawing transient, uninformed flow rather than a stable institutional clientele, which corresponds to noisier pricing that is more prone to short-term reversal.

A bounded fraction of recent trading value that came on up-days vs down-days proxies which side has dominated order flow; sustained one-sided volume reflects accumulation or distribution that continues beyond what the return series alone shows.

Aggregate price range generated per aggregate dollar traded over the same window is a price-impact proxy: names needing more range to absorb a given amount of trading value are structurally less liquid and should carry an illiquidity premium.

Volatility of returns measured only on above-average-volume days separates information-driven volume surges (large accompanying price moves) from mechanical liquidity-driven ones like block trades or index flows, which carry different forward-return implications.

Crosses a stock's baseline liquidity standing among peers with its own recent volume-acceleration rank; an otherwise-typical-liquidity name suddenly accelerating trading relative to its own history flags a regime change a static level alone would miss.

Both legs are scaled to each stock's own recent history before combining, so a high ratio means today's move is unusually large relative to how unusual today's volume is for that name: a thin-liquidity move achieved without much volume, which tends to partly revert.

A spike-resistant count of days trading above a stock's own six-month baseline distinguishes a durable liquidity-regime shift, such as new index inclusion or sustained attention, from a single volume outlier that a magnitude-based stat would overweight.

Net intraday directional move per unit of recent trading value: a large net move achieved on modest trading value indicates informed flow the order book absorbs efficiently, a liquidity signature distinct from wick- or full-range-based illiquidity measures.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21)) accepted at 4.998 with no fundamental leg at all, the round's second-best. The winning assignment put TS_RANK on the leg that varies within a name over time and CS_RANK on a cross-sectional dispersion stat of the other leg; don't default to requiring a fundamental partner in every price/volume product.
  2. TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, 21), 21) accepted at 4.507. Rank-transforming the volume leg is what rescues a return/volume correlation; raw-return-vs-raw-volume stays a dead end, but the fix is TS_RANK on volume, not abandoning the pairing.
  3. The fundamental-minus-raw-leg rank spread set a new round-best (6.794, EPS minus a bounded price-position ratio); keep exploring bounded price ratios as the 'other' leg, not just volume/range ranks. The one spread that failed did so on coverage from a 252-day window on the non-fundamental leg, not the fundamental choice; cap any window in a spread at 63 days regardless of which leg carries it.
  4. Two crossover children were rejected for donating only 2 shared nodes from a normal 5-node parent instead of exactly 3, both against the same RANK($roa) * RANK($dollar_volume) parent, both replacing one whole branch and keeping only the other operator-plus-leaf pair. Target an exactly-3-node shared subtree with each parent, not a whole branch or a single leaf.
  5. TS_DELTA($close, w) as a standalone or multiplied-in displacement leg failed cheap_screen 4x this round (|t| 0.08-0.56, incl. ABS(TS_DELTA($close,15))/range and two CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($close,3))*... variants); TS_DELTA($volume,3) played the same 'delta ingredient' role inside 2 accepts (1.383, 0.867) instead — prefer volume deltas over close deltas.
  6. Wrapping only the volume argument of an already-archived TS_CORR(x, $volume, w) in TS_RANK does not decorrelate: TS_CORR(TS_STD($return,5), TS_RANK($volume,21), 21) hit rho 0.857 and TS_CORR(TS_RANK($volume,10), $high-$low, 10) hit rho 0.809, both against raw-$volume archive parents with different partner terms and windows.
  7. TS_STD($high-$low,63)/(TS_STD($high-$low,5)+1e-8) alone failed cheap_screen (|t| 0.86) — this vol-term-structure ratio only cleared before when crossed with a momentum/delta multiplier (prior 6.583 accept); don't resubmit the bare ratio.
  8. $return-driven kernels failed cheap_screen again this round (TS_CORR($return,...) 0.26, ABS($return)*TS_DELTA(TS_RANK($volume,...),...) 0.42) — still the weakest primary leg available.
  9. TS_RANK($high-$low,21) is archive-blocked under any outer wrapper (collided both inside a CS_RANK($accrual_gap)* product and inside a TS_CORR(...,126) with volume rank); the stochastic ($close-TS_MIN($low,21))/(X($high,21)-TS_MIN($low,21)) chassis is now closed for X = TS_MAX or EMA. Move to a different window or range statistic, not a smoothing-function swap.
  10. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63)) was this round's best fitness (3.713) — nesting TS_RANK inside the non-fundamental leg of a rank-spread still clears correlation against flatter versions; this template still has room.
  11. CS_RANK($roa) * TS_RANK($high-$low,5) scored 3.149 (2nd best) — short-window (5-day) range-rank crossed with a fundamental rank is still open, unlike the saturated 21/63-day range windows.
  12. 3 of 20 rejects (15%) this round were exact within-run duplicates — diff new proposals against the full batch already proposed this run, not just the archive.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
